title: [UI/UX] Recovery Potential Flag — Dependency
walkthroughSteps: Navigate to /claims/CLM-2024-001/overview — the Recovery potential card now asks the Yes/No question directly on the card, no modal

walkthroughSteps.title: Recovery potential
walkthroughSteps.body: Yes/No radios sit on the card itself. Before the Recoveries call this was a modal behind a link labelled "Set", and handlers read it as optional — so it went unanswered and recoverable money left with the closed claim.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: Picking No reveals a required reason field; picking Yes enables Save and, once saved, surfaces a Set up recovery case link.

walkthroughSteps.title: Save is a deliberate second click
walkthroughSteps.body: The radios do not commit on selection. This field gates claim closure, so a misclick should be recoverable before it is written to the activity log.
walkthroughSteps.expectedAfterClick: The chip in the card header updates and the activity log records the old and new value.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Yes/No radios are on the Claim Overview card, not behind a modal
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The **Recovery potential** card renders **Yes/No radios directly on screen** with a **Save** action. The old Set/Update modal is gone.

setup.description: CLM-2024-001 carries a decided No by default — no override needed

preconditions.text: Recovery potential card shows Yes/No radios inline
No Set/Update link and no modal

expectedUI.description: Radios and a Save button render on the card body
visualCues: Question "Is recovery possible on this claim?" above the radios
Yes / No radios side by side
Save is disabled until the selection differs from what is on record
Chip in the card header reflects the saved answer

howToTest.trigger: Scroll to the Recovery potential card
howToTest.expectedResult: Yes/No radios are visible without clicking anything

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An unanswered claim says so on the card
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: With no answer on record the card shows a **warning message** and a **left accent border** — not the silent `–` it used to render.

setup.description: Blank the seeded answer on CLM-2024-001 to reach the unanswered state

preconditions.text: Warning message on the Recovery potential card

visualCues: "A Yes/No recovery decision is required before this claim can be closed."
Left accent border in the warning colour
No chip in the card header
Radios render unselected

howToTest.expectedResult: Card carries a warning message and an accent border

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An unanswered claim cannot be closed
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: The pre-closure checklist has a **Recovery potential answered** row that fails while the question is unanswered, so **Continue stays disabled**.

setup.description: Same unanswered state as AC-02, on a claim whose other blockers are all clear

preconditions.text: Close Claim opens the modal at Step 1 with a recovery-potential blocker

visualCues: Blocker "Recovery potential has not been answered (Yes/No)"
"Answer on Claim Overview" deep-link on the blocker row
Checklist row "Recovery potential answered" is not ticked

howToTest.expectedResult: Modal opens at Step 1 listing the recovery-potential blocker; Continue is disabled

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Answering No requires a reason, and then closure is no longer held up
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: Selecting **No** reveals a **required** reason field. Once saved, the closure blocker clears — *"if they select no, the pressure is off"*.

setup.description: Identical to AC-03 except the seeded No is left on record — the only difference between the two is the answer, so canClose flipping to true isolates this blocker

preconditions.text: Reason field is required when No is selected
Saved reason renders under the radios

expectedUI.description: Reason textarea with a validation error when empty
visualCues: "Why is no recovery expected?" textarea appears on selecting No
"A reason is required when recovery potential is No." on an empty save
No chip in the card header once saved
Checklist row "Recovery potential answered" is ticked

howToTest.trigger: Select No, clear the reason, click Save
howToTest.expectedResult: Validation error blocks the save; filling the reason saves and clears the closure blocker

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Yes with no recovery case routes the handler to the recovery domain
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: **Yes** on its own is not enough — the card surfaces a **Set up recovery case** link, and the closure modal warns that no recovery case exists. **NOTE [accepted-deviation]:** the link and the warning are built, but `/claims/:id/recoveries` is still a redirect stub (`app.routes.ts`) — the handler is *pointed at* the recovery domain rather than landed in it. This state is also deliberately a soft warning, not a hard closure blocker: a hard blocker whose fix-it link dead-ends would be unresolvable. Promoting it ships with the real recoveries surface — kept `partial` until then.

setup.description: Yes on record with no recovery case. CLM-2024-024 is seeded this way for the dashboard prompt; here the state is patched onto the target claim so the assertion runs against it

preconditions.text: Recovery potential is Yes with no recovery case

acceptanceCriteria.statement: The dashboard chases the decision without task management
acceptanceCriteria.plainStatement: A **Recovery potential: decision needed** panel on the dashboard lists open claims with no answer, plus claims answered Yes that have no recovery case — *"maybe we do it from dashboard even"*.
